adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 — [P1 confidence=100] `host = uri.host` discards the port accepted and retained by host validation, so a saved `example.com:8080` mapping never matches `http://example.com:8080/post`, denying embedding and losing its category selection.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the diff, the EmbeddableHost model validates hosts with a regex that allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), and the before_validation strips http/https and paths but preserves the port in the stored host. However, in record_for_host method (line 14), `host = uri.host` extracts only the hostname without the port (URI#host returns just the host, not host:port). This means if an admin saves 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, when checking if a URL like 'http://example.com:8080/post' is allowed, the lookup will search for 'example.com' (without port) which won't match 'example.com:8080' stored in the database. This is a correctness bug that would cause embedding to fail for hosts with non-standard ports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — [advisory P2 confidence=75] `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];` followed by `delete obj[k];` erases every original relationship-ID array even when its sideloaded collection is absent, so a REST serializer returning IDs without embedded records leaves consumers with undefined relationships and no recoverable IDs; although the new embedding serializer supplies its collection, this shared-store rule applies to every REST-serialized model and should preserve unresolved IDs as the singular branch already does.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in the diff. Looking at lines 196-210 in store.js.es6, when handling plural IDs (m[2] is truthy for '_ids' suffix), the code does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];` followed by `delete obj[k];`. The hydrated array is created by mapping over obj[k] and calling _lookupSubType for each ID. If _lookupSubType returns undefined/null for any ID (because the sideloaded collection is absent), those entries become undefined in the array. More critically, the original IDs are always deleted regardless of whether hydration succeeded. In contrast, the singular branch (else clause) only deletes obj[k] when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated)`). This asymmetry means plural relationships lose their original IDs even when sideloaded data is missing, while singular relationships preserve them. This is a real behavioral inconsistency that could cause bugs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the save action. Looking at lines 35-38 of embeddable-host.js.es6, after `host.save(props)` resolves in the `.then()` callback, the code reads `this.get('categoryId')` to set the category on the host object. However, `categoryId` is bound to the category-chooser component (line 6 of the template shows `{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}`), and the save button only disables based on `cantSave` (which checks `isSaving` and empty host), not the category chooser. If a user changes the category selection while the save request is in flight, the displayed category after save will be the newly selected one, not the one that was actually persisted (which was captured in `props.category_id` before the async call).

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that port and case-insensitive validation forms are unverified, but looking at the diff: 1) The EmbeddableHost model uses a case-insensitive regex with /i flag and the lookup uses 'lower(host)' in SQL, so case handling is built-in. 2) The validation regex explicitly allows ports with '(:[0-9]{1,5})?' pattern. 3) The test in spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb tests the host_allowed? method with http/https variations which exercises the record_for_host lookup.
